claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.note: This describes the contents of an answer, not the procedure for filing it.

claims.claim: A general denial is allowed in some limited civil cases.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is the short general-denial form.
claims.note: PLD-050 was named but not provided.

claims.claim: Limited civil cases are claims of $35,000 or less.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The ceiling is necessary, not sufficient. The amount excludes attorneys’ fees, interest, and costs; subdivisions (b) and (c) also restrict the relief sought.

claims.claim: PLD-050 says it cannot be used for a claim over $1,000 assigned to someone else for collection.
claims.note: The form is missing. CCP-431.30(d) contains no $1,000 threshold and conditions its assigned-claim exception on verification.

claims.claim: Many debt buyer lawsuits meet the stated amount and assignment conditions.
claims.note: No source establishes how often debt buyer suits meet either condition.

claims.claim: An assigned collection claim over $1,000 requires a more specific answer.
claims.quote: However, if the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1.
claims.note: The statutory exception requires a verified complaint as well as assignment for collection. It specifies how to deny allegations, without a dollar threshold.

claims.claim: You should get help with the response if that is your case.
If you cannot afford the filing fee, ask for a fee waiver.
claims.note: No fee-waiver eligibility or procedure text was provided.

claims.claim: FW-001 is the form for requesting the waiver.
claims.note: FW-001 was named but not provided.

flags.text: The draft treats amount and assignment alone as requiring a more specific denial. Section 431.30(d) makes verification material.
The $35,000 ceiling alone does not define a limited civil case.
The actual PLD-050 restriction, filing instructions, fee-waiver instructions, and prevalence claim remain unverified.
“If that is your case” directs an individual reader toward a specific response and recommends getting help.
Relying on an unchecked form restriction or on debt-buyer status without checking assignment and verification could lead to an improper denial, a defective response, and a risk of default.

result.summary: The statutes support the dollar ceiling and conditional use of a general denial. They do not establish the draft’s form-selection rule, and the draft omits verification from the assigned-claim exception.
